title: Request Bonsai: Sprint Lattice (Jan 19 2026)
content:
One-page synth (working): a compact harvest of customer asks and early prioritization for a small sprint of low-risk, high-customer-visibility patches. Using the 'bonsai' metaphor: small targeted pruning and wiring that reduces friction for heavy-usage customers while we design larger trunk-level changes (dedicated / private rollout flows).

Context and intent
- Quick synthesis from 6 CS calls + 4 inbound tickets (Jan 5–15). Focus: runtime/friction signals that block adoption of Dedicated and Private tiers and cause support escalations for Hosted customers hitting cost/latency surprises.
- Goal: identify 3 fast probes (2-week picks) that will materially reduce support load or unblock a pilot. Also sketch 1 medium project (quarter) to push into eng roadmap.
- Not exhaustive; this is intentionally tactical and customer-anchored.

Raw vignettes (paraphrased)
1) FinHealth startup: "We got hit with a huge bill after enabling streaming — tokens looked fine on the dashboard but there was no per-request breakdown; our engineers had to pause traffic." Wants token-level per-request cost exposure and an alert when per-route spend exceeds X/day.
2) Retail analytics vendor on Dedicated pilot: "Autoscaling oscillates at spike boundaries; some inference calls fall back to smaller models unexpectedly and latency jumps." Wants clearer routing & fallback visibility and a knob to prefer capacity reservation over immediate fallback.
3) Platform integrator using Private VPC: "Key rotation tested poorly — some nodes lost access to KMS and requests errored with 500s; audit logs were fragmented across systems." Wants a preflight KMS/secret-check tool and unified audit traces per-request.
4) Gaming partner: "KV-cache misses on repeated prompt prefixes — we suspect client SDK not pinning conversation ids; costs grow with repeated context." Wants default-client patterns + an SDK opt-in that enforces stable conversation IDs and exposes cache-hit telemetry.
5) Marketplace customer: "We need canary controls for function/tool calling so we can test a new tool without exposing it to all tenants. Right now rollouts are coarse." Wants per-tenant canary routing and rollback that’s visible in Console.

Synthesis: common threads
- Observability gaps: token-level per-request cost, per-route and per-tenant rollout visibility, cache-hit/miss telemetry, and unified request traces spanning control plane and private deployments.
- Routing & fallback clarity: customers want predictable degradation (favor reserved capacity or queued requests over silent fallback to smaller models) and explicit policy knobs (latency vs cost preference).
- Private deployment reliability: preflight checks and unified audit logs are top asks before pilots scale — KMS, networking, and node health checks need to be tightened.
- Small developer ergonomics: SDKs and defaults (conversation IDs, streaming toggles) can reduce accidental cost/latency patterns.

Proposed 3 quick probes (2 weeks each)
A) Token-by-request mini-dashboard + alert prototype
- What: add per-request token and cost breakdown in Console for the last 7 days and a new alert rule: "route X exceeds $Y/day". Surface streaming cost attribution separately.
- Why: directly addresses high-bill surprise; low infra risk (aggregate data already exists in billing pipeline). Big customer visibility.
- Acceptance: demo to FinHealth customer; no perf impact; Jira: JIRA-CS-1729.

B) KV-cache instrumentation + SDK opt-in
- What: lightweight telemetry (cache hit/miss, key-stability warnings) instrumented in runtime and an SDK flag that enforces stable conversation IDs and returns cache metrics in response headers.
- Why: cuts repeated token spend in scenarios like chat bots and gaming where prefixes repeat.
- Acceptance: 10% drop in token spend on repeat-prefix synthetic workload; partner test with Gaming customer.

C) Canary routing toggle (Console UI + API) for tool/function exposures
- What: per-tenant simple toggle and percentage rollout for tool/function calling and model variants, with immediate console visibility and rollback button.
- Why: reduces friction for marketplace partners and integrators testing risky tool integrations.
- Acceptance: used by Marketplace customer for a live canary; telemetry shows <2% incorrect exposures.

Medium project (quarter) — "Pruned Routing & Visibility"
- Bundle: formalize routing policy UI and API (latency vs cost preferences), explicit fallback chain config, and a per-request unified trace that ties control-plane decisions (fallbacks, routing) to the runtime traces and billing records. Includes a Private preflight KMS/network health check CLI and a server-side audit joiner that emits a single trace id across infra and control plane.
- Impact: enables safe Dedicated rollouts, reduces unexpected fallback escalations, and delivers enterprise-ready audit trails for Private.
- Risks: cross-team (runtime, console, billing, private infra) coordination; needs schema for trace joiner and performance testing for trace sampling.

Low-friction quick fixes / heuristics (tickets to spin up)
- Add a "streaming token cost" line item to invoices and expose in per-route breakdown (billing team; quick UI patch).
- Console banner when a route has >30% fallback rate in last hour (ops signal to Product).
- SDK release note: recommend stable conversation id pattern and give example wrapper function; add a small snippet in quickstart.
- Private preflight checklist: show missing KMS policies, expired certs, and node clock drift warnings.

Open questions / notes to self
- How fresh is per-request cost data in billing pipeline? Is near-real-time feasible without heavy load? (ask billing infra)
- For cache telemetry: sample vs full instrumentation? Full might add noise to logging and cost — propose header-level minimal metrics first.
- Rollback UX: do teams want instant abort (stop new traffic) or graceful ramp-down? Need SRE input.
- Trace joiner spec: what fields must survive between control plane and runtime? conversation_id, request_id, model_variant, tenant_id, fallback_reason — validate with Private infra team.

Next steps (owners & timeline)
- Maya: create Jira seed tickets for probes A/B/C and link artifacts (this doc) — due 2026-01-21.
- Rafael (CS): schedule demo with FinHealth and Gaming customers for early feedback — due 2026-01-27.
- Priya (Product): sync with Billing and Runtime leads on feasibility of token-by-request data latency — schedule 30-min on 2026-01-22.
- Ethan (Solutions Eng): draft Private preflight CLI spec & list of checks — deliver draft 2026-02-02.

Quick links and references
- CONFLUENCE: kv-cache-primer (internal)
- JIRA: JIRA-CS-1729 (token-breakdown alert seed)
- GH: GH-PR-4512 (SDK conversation-id wrapper prototype)

End notes (rough)
- This is intentionally pragmatic: three small visible wins + one medium cross-cutting project. Keep probes narrow and measurable. If any probe shows quick lift with partner(s), we should prioritize backlog grooming with eng leads for Q2.
- Unresolved: sampling cadence for traces and billing pipeline latency. Will follow up in Prod-Billing sync.

-- maya (notes)
